about: Per-stock build recipe for tools/film_profiles/build.py, as data/profile-sources/kodak-e190/recipe.json; see README.md. Source: EASTMAN EXR 100T Color Negative Film 5248/7248, KODAK Publication No. H-1-7248, March 1999. Charts are vector polylines on tick-marked or gridded frames, drawn as E-190 (extract_pdf.py options ticks, polyline, grid_width, frame_any_re); the characteristic chart carries log lux-seconds on its top edge and camera stops on its bottom edge, and only the top scale is used (tick_edges, tick_straddle).

kodak_exr_100t.name: Kodak EXR 100T
kodak_exr_100t.window_prior_reason: at the default 0.002 the fit put c_uv at 389.1 nm, under the shipped windows' range (391-456; D8 check 10); 0.003 is the smallest of 0.003/0.004/0.006/0.01 that passes, giving [394.4, 21.5, 610.4, 59.2] at a corpus loss 2 % above the unconstrained fit (0.0215 against 0.0211; no window 0.0276).
kodak_exr_100t.datasheet_heading: EASTMAN EXR 100T Color Negative Film 5248/7248 (H-1-7248, March 1999): Characteristic Curves (tungsten 1/50 s, ECN-2, Status M), Spectral-Sensitivity Curves (effective exposure 0.013 s, 0.40 above D-min, Status M), Spectral-Dye-Density Curves (midscale neutral and D-min, ECN-2)
notes: The characteristic chart has two exposure scales: log lux-seconds on top (ticks 3-bar.0 to 1.0, labelled at both frame edges) and camera stops below. They disagree by 9 % (one drawn stop is 0.276 log10 H on the top scale, not 0.301). The curves are read on the top scale, the sensitometric one, which gives a green mid-scale gamma of about 0.59; the stop scale would give about 0.54.
